correctness.rationale: On a compact invariant flow, invariant generator integrals of antiderivatives F(x) and K(y) give E[y|x]=0 and E[x|y]=a(1-y^(2n))y (a.e.); F(x)=x²/2 also gives E[xy]=0. H=(x²+y²)/2 satisfies L H=a y²(1-y^(2n)), proving E[y^(2n+2)]=E[y²] since a≠0. The second fiber regression has residual -ydot orthogonal to every y-measurable function; total variance yields Var(x)=Var(a(1-y^(2n))y)+E[ydot²]. Strict convexity of Z^(n+1), Z=y², gives E[y²]≤1, with zero implying only origin support, and equality-one impossible because |y|=1 along a full invariant orbit would force x=0 and simultaneously xdot=±1. A zero averaged signed pumping term not supported only at y=0,±1 forces occupation on both sides |y|=1. Positive x/y variances for nonorigin states give exact Corr=0; periodic continuity gives ≥2 crossings per least period. Rechecked the algebra independently; packaged verify.py merely tests rational instances, not these analytic support arguments.
